subject: English
passage: While completing graduate research in Boston in the 1990s, Priya Ito found that tropical microbial ecosystems were rarely featured in the leading microbiology journals, despite Boston's standing as a global center for microbiome science. According to science writer Ramiro Espinoza, later in her career as an influential journal editor, Ito sought to remedy this gap, not by devoting special issues solely to tropical microbiomes, but by showing how research on those ecosystems fit into the broader picture of worldwide microbial diversity and ecological theory.
prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Espinoza's claim?

choices.A: As editor of the journal Microbial Frontiers, Ito commissioned an extensive special issue devoted entirely to the gut microbiomes of Amazonian amphibians, one of the most comprehensive treatments of a single tropical microbial system ever published.
choices.B: In the collection Global Microbiomes in Comparison, 1995–2015, Ito and coeditor Hanna Reinhardt brought together studies of tropical microbial communities from regions such as Borneo alongside prominent work from temperate and polar systems, including Swedish boreal soils and Antarctic dry valleys.
choices.C: Ito's editorial work on the 2003 volume Microbes and Postcolonial Land Reform in the Tropics, 1950–2000 showed how political transitions following independence in tropical nations reshaped agricultural practices and, in turn, the microbial communities studied by researchers such as Felipe Carrera and Nadia Osei.
choices.D: Ito edited the collection Sampling Approaches in Tropical Microbiology, 1990 to the Present not to champion any single methodology but to showcase the wide variety of techniques tropical researchers have used to characterize microbial communities.

explanation:
Choice B is the best answer because it presents a finding that, if true, would most directly support science writer Ramiro Espinoza's claim about Ito's editorial work. Espinoza asserts that Ito sought not just to feature tropical microbiomes on their own but to show 'how research on those ecosystems fit into the broader picture of worldwide microbial diversity and ecological theory.' The description of Global Microbiomes in Comparison, 1995–2015 indicates that Ito and Reinhardt's collection brought studies of tropical microbial communities together with prominent work on temperate and polar systems from other regions, thus supporting Espinoza's claim that Ito sought to place tropical microbiome research within a global scientific context.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect because it describes a special issue that would not support Espinoza's claim that Ito wanted to show how tropical microbial research fits into the broader context of worldwide microbial science. The description of the special issue indicates that it focused entirely on a single tropical system — the gut microbiomes of Amazonian amphibians. The description does not suggest that the issue showed how that system fit into a global scientific context.
